body_markdown:
Four-time F1 World Champion[Max Verstappen](https://www.hagerty.com/media/tags/max-verstappen/) returned to his racing roots by battling a field of 100 kart racers.


Staged yesterday at Kart Silverstone in the U.K., the Max vs 100 event pitted Verstappen against 100 competitors in identical machinery. The Red Bull Racing driver started at the back of the field and was tasked with making his way through the pack.


Racing against him were athletes and social media influencers with a combined reach of half a billion followers, while the race was streamed live on Disney +. The rules stated that any driver who was passed by Verstappen had to retire to the pit lane and not try to fight to regain position. The organizers estimated that it would take the champ 30 laps, or 75 minutes, to challenge for the lead.


Mihai Stetcu / Red Bull Content Pool


That was not the case, however, as Verstappen breezed past opposition that mostly had little to no racing experience. On the first lap alone Verstappen made up more than 60 places, largely thanks to an almighty pile-up. After that initial carnage, which wiped out two-thirds of the field, Verstappen swiftly made his way through the pack. By lap four he was in the top 20; on lap six he’d reached the top ten.


At this point the competition was a little more serious, with the likes of[Larry Chen](https://www.hagerty.com/media/tags/larry-chen/) , YouTuber Zac Alsop, Red Bull Ford Powertrains technician Lewis Osler, and Dutch F1 journalist Jacky Martens putting up a bit more of a fight. Verstappen’s pace was unmatched, however, and after just 14 laps and 35 minutes he took the checkered flag.


“Simply lovely,” said Verstappen, who first drove a kart at the age of four and won the European Karting Championship at 15. “It was great to just be back in a go-kart again and go back to basics—it reminded me of racing back in the day. It’s a really beautiful track and well designed, and it was a nice touch to be able to get all the data fed through the radio, too. I had a great day, and it was good to come out with the win!”
